root_cause: GitHub-hosted Actions blob storage backend returned HTTP 503 'Egress is over the account limit' repeatedly (5 retries each) when multiple jobs in this run attempted to download large build/test artifacts (openvino_js_package, openvino_tests, openvino package) concurrently. This is a GitHub-side infrastructure egress throttling condition, not a code or configuration defect in the repository. All affected jobs failed at the artifact-download step before any OpenVINO-specific code ran, and the overall Windows status job failed solely because of these cascading upstream failures.
reproduction_steps: N/A - this is a transient GitHub Actions infrastructure egress-throttling condition on blob storage that cannot be reproduced locally. It typically clears after retrying the run once GitHub's account-level egress quota resets.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed jobs later (outside this doctor's scope - report only); egress throttling is usually transient and resolves once account egress quota resets.

If this recurs frequently, consider reducing total artifact egress per run (e.g., trimming artifact sizes, enabling compression, or staggering/parallelism limits for jobs that download large artifacts simultaneously).
Monitor GitHub Actions status page and the organization's Actions artifact egress usage/quota dashboard for recurring account-level throttling.
Consider raising a support ticket with GitHub if this pattern recurs across many runs in a short window, since it indicates the org may be near its artifact egress cap.
prevention_strategies: Reduce simultaneous large-artifact downloads across parallel jobs in post-commit pipelines, keep artifact sizes minimal (prune unnecessary files before upload), and consider caching/download backoff tuning. Since this is an account-level GitHub infrastructure limit, the most durable mitigation is monitoring artifact egress volume per run/day and spreading heavy jobs across time where possible.
historical_context: No prior post-commit investigation in this knowledge base recorded this exact 'Egress is over the account limit' blob-storage 503 signature. Related but distinct network/infrastructure patterns exist in the database (e.g., ENOTFOUND/ECONNREFUSED artifact upload failures, codeload.github.com resource-unavailable errors, DNS resolution failures), all categorized as Network/Infrastructure, confirming that GitHub Actions infra-level transient failures are a recurring theme though this specific egress-cap signature is new.
